result:
**REST wins on simplicity, GraphQL on client flexibility.**

REST: resource-per-URL, plain HTTP semantics → HTTP caching (CDN, ETags) works free, easy to debug with curl, rate-limit per endpoint, mature tooling, auth per route. Costs: over-fetching/under-fetching, multiple round trips for nested data, endpoint sprawl or versioning as clients diverge.

GraphQL: one endpoint, client specifies exact shape → no over-fetch, one round trip, typed schema doubles as docs/codegen, good for many varied clients (web, mobile). Costs: caching is hard (everything is POST to `/graphql`, needs persisted queries or client-side normalized cache), N+1 resolver problem (needs DataLoader), query-cost attacks (deep/wide queries → need depth limits, complexity analysis, timeouts), per-field authorization, file uploads awkward, more upfront learning and infra, errors return 200 with an `errors` array → monitoring is harder.

Verdict: default to REST for a new API with few clients, public/third-party consumers, or a small team. Pick GraphQL when multiple frontends need different data shapes from a deeply relational model, and you can afford the ops overhead. Can add GraphQL later as a gateway over REST services, so starting with REST is the lower-regret choice.
